sn19.14:1.1: _Maṅguli_ is unclear. It is perhaps related to _maṅgura_ as a skin color, neither black nor brown, where the corresponding Sanskrit term is _madgura_, also spelled _maṅgura_. This is a species of fish, probably the common catfish *clarias magur*, which has a dingy greenish or muddy color.
sn19.14:1.4: _Ikkhaṇikā_ (Sanskrit _īkṣaṇikā_)is a “fortune teller” or “seer”. What she sees are _maṅgala_ (“auspicies”), hence she is reborn like a _maṅguli_ (“catfish”). She is mentioned 13.1.7 Such fortune-tellers were considered a “thorn” to the society  as a “thorn” alongside dissemblers, cheats and gamblers, and palmists (Manu 9.258). Medhātithi comments that they would con wealthy men out of money buy promising them the favors of the gods.
